method: The 37 testbed targets + 2 clean-host baselines in corpus.expanded.json are the ground truth: each setup.sh plants one uniquely-named, known privilege-escalation misconfiguration. Z-Privesc detection = the planted artifact's unique signature appears in the probe's JSON findings with a DETERMINISTIC verdict. 35 targets evaluated on Kali WSL2; kernel_hardening and process_root evaluated on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (multipass VM) because WSL2 locks sysctls and kills background processes.
environment: 35 targets: Kali WSL2 (kali-linux), kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, root. 2 targets (kernel_hardening, process_root): Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (multipass zp-2204), kernel 5.15.0-185-generic, root. Z-Privesc run as root (the intended defensive operator).

zp_false_positive_proxy.note: On a clean Kali WSL2 host, Z-Privesc reports 78 ambient findings (system SUID binaries, capabilities, polkit, etc.) — these are real system state, not misclassifications. Zero false positives on the 37 planted targets.

kali_wsl2.note: All 35 targets planted and detected on Kali WSL2

ubuntu_2204_multipass.note: kernel_hardening (6 sysctl findings) and process_root (1 PROC-WW finding) verified on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS multipass VM

gtfobins_baseline.note: GTFOBins covers 32/37 techniques as documented knowledge but performs zero automated presence-detection.

interpretation: Z-Privesc achieves 100% recall (37/37) on planted, uniquely-identifiable misconfigurations with 0 false positives on planted targets. Path recall is 94.3% (33/35 root-reachable targets with correct root paths identified). Two targets (kernel_hardening, process_root) were evaluated on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (multipass) due to WSL2 limitations (locked sysctls, background process lifecycle). GTFOBins covers 86.5% of techniques as knowledge but provides zero automated scan recall.
